identity.summary: Ruinlokaliteten etter Clemenskirken i middelalder-Oslo, med bevart steinkirkeruin og eldre gravnivåer på stedet.

coordinate.coordNote: Geometrisk representasjonspunkt beregnet fra Riksantikvarens offisielle MultiPolygon-geometri for Clemenskirken kirkested, Kulturminne-ID 51949. Punktet representerer den konkrete kirke-/ruinlokaliteten og ikke Middelalderparken som helhet.

duplicateGate.conclusion: No canonical Clemenskirken ruin identity exists. The nearby records represent a historic house, the broad Middelalderparken anchor, Mariakirken and Hallvardskirken as separate physical identities.

documentedCore: Riksantikvaren identifies locality 51949 as Clemenskirken kirkested in Oslo municipality 0301.
The surviving stone church is a two-aisled medieval church ruin; the registry dates its building phase probably to the 1130s–1140s.
Older burial levels at the site reach back to around year 1000 and support earlier church phases, but no older church structure has been directly demonstrated.
The church was abandoned and demolished after the Reformation; the ruin was excavated in 1920–1921 and conserved/reconstructed in connection with the 2000 millennium works.
avoid: Do not present an earlier timber church as archaeologically proven when the evidence is burial levels and inference.
Do not merge the ruin into the broad Middelalderparken place.
Do not confuse Clemenskirken with Mariakirken or Hallvardskirken.
